source.title: Memorization and Optimization in Deep Neural Networks with Minimum Over-parameterization
source.authors: Simone Bombari; Mohammad Hossein Amani; Marco Mondelli

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves and experimentally illustrates that gradient descent can drive training loss to zero for deep networks under minimum over-parameterization, using a theoretical NTK analysis and a regression loss rather than benchmark classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a theorem for least-squares training and an Adam experiment on Gaussian inputs and targets. It does not test CIFAR classification, random labels, or the failure conditions in the versions. Figure 1 reports NTK eigenvalue measurements, which do not directly measure the claim's training-error outcomes and are omitted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves and illustrates convergence of fully connected networks on real-valued regression targets. V1 concerns convolutional networks' training classification error on CIFAR-10/100. The study does not test that outcome or any other listed version; its initialization construction alone does not test V4's speed or trainable-depth comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish NTK eigenvalue bounds under minimum over-parameterization and derive memorization and gradient-descent optimization guarantees. Zero-loss convergence requires their chosen initialization and theorem assumptions; it is not established for standard initialization generally.
record.recipe_differences: Uses NTK eigenvalue bounds and a specially constructed duplicated-neuron initialization to prove regression optimization; illustrative experiment uses Adam, Gaussian inputs and targets, and reports loss rather than classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: The optimization guarantee uses a chosen initialization with duplicated neurons, boosted final-layer variance γ = d³N², and a learning-rate upper bound; the experiment uses Adam.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4 guarantees geometric convergence to zero least-squares loss under smooth-activation, data, topology and width assumptions, using a specially constructed initialization and a bounded learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep fully connected networks can fit real-valued targets by gradient descent with roughly linear parameter count, up to logarithmic factors, under specified assumptions and initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: The Gaussian-input, Gaussian-target experiment reports a transition from loss around 1 to approximately zero as four-layer ReLU networks reach widths of order sqrt(N), using Adam and averaging ten trials.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Four-layer fully connected ReLU networks trained with Adam can interpolate Gaussian regression targets when their parameter count is sufficiently large relative to sample count.

record.problems: The theoretical training guarantee is restricted to least-squares regression, specific data and smooth-activation assumptions, minimum over-parameterization, and a specially chosen initialization. The illustrative experiment uses Gaussian data and targets, and its precise values are only in a plot; it does not evaluate classification benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 reports smallest NTK eigenvalues for sigmoid networks and is not a training-error outcome. Other theorem-level NTK and memorization-capacity statements do not report gradient-training outcomes for this claim.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks trained on CIFAR-10/100; training classification error with clean, corrupted or random labels; smaller-model, early-stopping and regularization conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum frequencies and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts; very deep tanh and Fixup alternatives.
Effects of activation-matched initialization on training speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and very deep convolutional networks.
Loss and curvature dynamics near or above the initial stability threshold, edge-of-stability training and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Neither regression result warrants a V1 verdict. Omission of CIFAR classification is an untested part, not evidence limiting V1. The NTK eigenvalue and memorization-existence results already declared in rows_left_out do not independently test any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Tests gradient descent reaching zero loss in a theoretical least-squares setting and an Adam experiment, but not classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, or comparisons involving smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes.

rows.subject: L-layer neural network (2.1)
rows.size_stated: Minimum over-parameterization: N·log⁸ N = o(nL−2 nL−1); nL−1 = O(N^γ) for some γ > 0.
rows.operation_detail: Least-squares gradient descent with the duplicated-neuron initialization in (4.2), γ = d³N², and η ≤ C(γNdnL−1)⁻¹.

conditions.value: N i.i.d. samples from PX satisfying Assumptions 1–2

rows.measure: training loss over gradient descent steps
rows.value: L(θt) ≤ (1 − cηγnL−2 nL−1)^t L(θ0), for all t ≥ 1; authors say this gives linear convergence to zero loss.
rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − C N e^(−c log² nL−1) − C e^(−c log² N); c and C are numerical constants
rows.note: The theorem is a regression/least-squares result with a specially constructed initialization; it does not report classification error.
rows.check: The least-squares convergence theorem does not measure V1's convolutional classification outcome. Correct the width condition to N^a = O(n_{L-1}) for some a > 0; the record reverses this inequality. Initialization is specially constructed with duplicated neurons, opposite output weights and boosted output-weight variance. The guarantee is theoretical, rather than an observed training run.

rows.subject: 4-layer ReLU network with d = n1 = n2 = n3
rows.size_stated: 4 layers; d = n1 = n2 = n3; Figure 2 plots against d² and N.
rows.operation_detail: Adam optimization on Gaussian inputs and targets; initialization follows the setting of Theorem 1 with βl = 1.
rows.measure: loss after gradient descent has converged
rows.uncertainty: plot averaged over 10 independent trials; no numerical error bars stated
rows.note: The text says the loss goes from 1 to 0 when layer widths are of order √N. Precise plotted values are figure-only.
rows.check: Gaussian-target regression loss in a fully connected ReLU network does not measure V1's classification outcome. The experiment uses Adam despite the figure caption's gradient-descent wording. Width and sample count vary across the plot; widths of order sqrt(N) describe the reported transition, not every plotted condition. Section 4 reports loss approaching zero, but precise cell values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
